name: Hunter Green
lede: Hunter green is a dark, slightly yellowish green, the kind of color a dictionary file puts near Hooker's and Lincoln green.

sections.title: What the dictionary says
sections.body: Paterson defines Hunter's green simply as a dark yellowish-green [1]. He lists it in the greens near Hooker's green and Lincoln green [2]. Hooker's green is documented more fully: a yellowy green first prepared from Prussian blue and gamboge, and now more often from cadmium yellow and phthalo blue [3]. No source in our books says who the hunter was, or when the name began [1][2].

sections.title: Not hunting pink
sections.body: Hunting pink, a few entries on in the same dictionary, names the coats of foxhunters, a different color and not a relative of this green [4].

sections.title: Neighbors
sections.body: In our list the close neighbors are [[forest-green]], [[dark-green]], [[kelly-green]] and [[emerald-green]] [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #355E3B measures lightness 36.1, chroma 27.7 and hue angle 145 degrees, which fits Paterson's wording of a dark green with a touch of yellow [1][5].
